headline: Zero top-rated coffee shops turn up in Ward 8, among the lowest counts in the city.
summary:
Ward 8 takes in Avalon Park, Pullman, Calumet Heights, and Chatham on Chicago's South Side. Ten wards finish behind Ward 8 in the overall standings, at rank 40. The score attached to that position is 34.38, closer to the middle of the pack than the bottom.

Coffee is the clearest weak spot. The ward sits near last citywide on coffee shops overall, on highly rated coffee shops, and on licensed coffee and tea shop density. Linguistic diversity ranks low too, reflecting a ward that is largely English-speaking. Child care runs in the opposite direction, well represented on two separate counts, and two modeled measures of religious belief and affiliation top the citywide list, though those come from statistical modeling rather than a survey of actual residents.
reading_the_rankings: Three numbers deserve a second look. Two points is all that separates Ward 8's 47th-place restaurant count from twelve other wards, so the rank overstates a real difference that barely exists. That restaurant count is also a ZIP code number wearing a ward's rank. ZIP boundaries don't track ward boundaries anywhere in the city, so the figure attached to Ward 8 is really an estimate borrowed from a different kind of map. Low confidence is the label the compiler puts on this count. Coffee shops tell a similar story. Two points is also the gap between Ward 8's coffee-shop count and eleven other wards, another rank that looks starker than the numbers underneath it. Coverage runs thin here too, since only some of the fifty wards have a reading for this measure at all, leaving the count that does exist thinner than a full citywide comparison would suggest. The top strength, a modeled estimate that 74 percent of adults are certain God exists, is not a survey finding. It's a model's projection, describing what a ward with these demographics tends to look like elsewhere in the country, not what residents here actually told anyone. The estimate's own publisher calls it low confidence.

news.headline: South Siders Still Waiting For Tree Cleanup After June Storms, But City Departments Are 'Overwhelmed'
news.note: City data showed the 8th Ward had more than 580 open tree-cleanup requests after June storms, the highest total of any Chicago ward.

alderperson.name: Michelle A. Harris
alderperson.verification_note: The website_url listed in the source data, aldermanmichelleharris.net, returned a Cloudflare bot-block on every fetch attempt this session and could not be verified directly. Fetched https://aldermanmichelleharris.com/ instead and confirmed it is her official site, including bio text stating Alderman Harris has lived in the 8th Ward for over fifty years. Cross-checked against the city's official ward page, https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/about/wards/08.html, which lists Alderman Michelle A. Harris for Ward 8, matching the name on file.
